item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It is worth mentioning that all the volcanoes on on Io are in fact Cryovolcanoes….

Unless Wikipedia is outright lying, the volcanoes on Io are not cryovolcanoes, but "regular" hot volcanoes spewing either basalt, sulfur, or ultramafic silicates. Io's heat comes from tidal forces due to its proximity to Jupiter and the effects of Europa and Ganymede on Io's orbit. To be sure, most of the volcanic objects in the outer Solar System are cryovolcanic, but Io is the exception because of its unique situation.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: It is worth mentioning that all the volcanoes on on Io are in fact Cryovolcanoes and are only operating at a temperature of 17° Celsius while the surrounding temperatures are around -143°. Therefore the cryovolcanoes are incapable of incinerating anything that we are familiar with. Does that mean that the volcanoes are vastly increasing their temperatures during the material drops or that the material being dropped is particularly vulnerable to 17° temperatures?

item.content:encoded:
Wormholes as garbage disposals, actually what they'd likely be used for by a race with the ability to generate them. Anything you can't recycle, you toss into a wormhole with the exit point above a black hole, star, or volcanic planetoid to be recycled cosmically. You'd need a monsterous amount of mass to appreciably alter whatever it is you're dumping into, and it lets you access the same dumping ground from potentially anywhere in the universe.

Oh, they'd be used for travel too, of course, but that's old hat.

It's occurred to me as well, that maybe this drop point is the other side of one or more of the SCPs the foundation chucks things into from time to time to see where they go.

a little better but still lacks a hook. a crapload of unknown matter appears mysteriously and is swiftly destroyed. something to keep away from public knowledge so uncomfortable questions dont get asked, but not any kind of apparent threat at this time.

the only real concern comes from humanity's advancing technology and the potential for people to one day not only know about this but to go and try to examine it. is this material dangerous in some way? if it did not get destroyed in the lava flow on the moon's surface or if it were disturbed in some way would it become a threat? if not then it seems most likely to be an example of wormholes in action, a scientific curiosity but something that's impossible to properly contain and mostly insignificant outside of throwing certain theories into chaos while advancing others.

downvoted for now as it currently exists because if i were the Foundation i wouldnt try to actively keep this secret yet. i'll check back if it changes though, and upvote if it improves enough. i do like the initial concept and the directions it could be taken.

item.content:encoded: Part of the problem is that Io is awash in radiation and Jupiter's magnetic field, so any craft that tries to orbit Io would likely be short-lived. Thus, the probes would more likely orbit Europa, the next moon out, or Jupiter in an orbit that would sometimes have it pass between Io and Jupiter. That would have been pointed out in the paragraph I cut, so between this and suggestions from the chat, it looks like I'll need to put it in after all.

item.content:encoded:
I always get a little anxious when specific real-world events are attributed to Foundation activity, but in this case it seems like it could serve a useful purpose. Currently, though, it is not.

If you have two orbital satellites actively monitoring this anomaly at relatively close range, it seems like we should have more information about it than just the period of appearance and the quantity. I dig the concept, but without any hint as to just what kind of stuff is getting dumped (which, by extension, could suggest where it might be coming from), the execution isn't fully satisfying. See if you can expand upon it in that direction a little more- this one's got plenty of potential.

I do enjoy the idea of some nefarious cosmic polluter using a moon volcano as a landfill, though, so tentatively upvoted.
